messages:
alex.h: FYI spotted weird RBAC behavior in private control plane today after the role-mapping refactor. Admin proxy is accepting connections from a stale conntrack entry and letting through admin-level requests.

maria: Wait, conntrack? Can you paste what you saw?

alex.h: short dump from the admin proxy host: 
```
# conntrack -L | grep 10.3.5.21
ipv4     2 tcp      6 431994 ESTABLISHED src=10.3.5.21 dst=10.0.20.9 sport=38012 dport=8443 packets=215 bytes=19872 src=10.0.20.9 dst=10.3.5.21 sport=8443 dport=38012 packets=210 bytes=20480 [ASSURED] mark=0
```
It appears the control-plane allowed the old source IP after an HA failover; mapping of cert->role is stale in the proxy cache, so requests were treated as superuser.

jordan: oof that maps to the onprem-admin certificate we rotate weekly. Did the rotation job run?

alex.h: rotation ran, but proxy cache didn't purge. I also see this in audit logs: 
```
2026-03-15T09:12:44Z admin-proxy request id=ab12 role=onprem-admin path=/v1/tenants/123/action method=POST auth=cert subject="CN=onprem-admin" allowed=true
```
requests after rotation should have been denied until reauth.

samir: Could be the RBAC refactor we deployed on 2026-03-14 that changed how subject CN maps to roles (we introduced group fallback). Maybe proxy cache key changed shapes.

maria: Can we confirm whether KMS signatures were revalidated? If cert was rotated but session cached, KMS-backed key check may have been skipped.

leo: I pulled the proxy service logs. There's a 2-line stacktrace around the cache invalidation path: 
```
2026-03-15T09:11:58Z cache: miss for key=cert:CN=onprem-admin
2026-03-15T09:11:58Z cache: insert key=cert://onprem-admin ttl=24h
2026-03-15T09:12:05Z role-mapper: map subject=CN=onprem-admin -> role=superuser (via group fallback)
2026-03-15T09:12:40Z cache: no invalidation triggered for rotation_event id=rot-7621
```

alex.h: tl;dr: rotation_event arrived but proxy didn't invalidate, so conntrack + cache kept the session alive. We need immediate mitigation.

jordan: mitigation options: 1) purge conntrack and restart proxy (disruptive), 2) push hotfix to invalidate cache on rotation_event, 3) patch role-mapper to prefer exact CN match.

samir: For incident short-term, we should purge conntrack and revoke the certs at KMS to be safe. Long-term: fix the cache invalidation and add automated audit alert if session reauth doesn't happen within X minutes after rotation.

leo: I'm wary of restarting proxy across all private deployments — that could interrupt active inference runs. Can we target only control-plane admin nodes?

maria: yes target admin proxy instances only. Also add a temporary nginx rule to reject requests with the old session cookie header until we fix cache.

samir: I'll trigger conntrack purge on affected hosts and call rotate/revoke on the KMS-managed cert (rot-7621). alex, can you coordinate?

alex.h: Starting now. Running: 
```bash
for host in admin-proxy-1 admin-proxy-2; do ssh $host sudo conntrack -D -s 10.3.5.21 || true; done
aws kms revoke --key-id alias/onprem-admin --revision rot-7621 || true
```

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-23 - admin-proxy stale-session allowed elevated access. Pager duty: oncall-eng-sre notified.

jordan: Post-mitigation notes: we purged conntrack and rotated the KMS key; audit logs show subsequent requests from that CN were denied as expected. Need a follow-up to add unit tests for cache invalidation and a regression eval.

leo: Also add alert in Redwood Console: alert when a cert rotation event occurs but >1 open session exists for that subject after 60s.

maria: I'll file a tracker. Action items: 
- samir: postmortem starter, timeline + scope (priv vs dedicated).
- alex.h: add hotfix PR to invalidate proxy cache on rotation_event.
- jordan: add conntrack purge runbook entry for private deployments.
- leo: console alert + eval.

samir: I'll own the postmortem. Quick question: do we need to notify any customers? Might affect dedicated/private tenants with onprem admin role.

alex.h: ops says we have 3 private tenants affected, they were briefly able to query admin-only endpoints but no config changes were made. Recommend notifying them with a short summary and mitigations.

maria: +1 to notify. Keep language precise: what happened, scope, actions taken, and follow-up. No immediate data exfil evidence.

leo: Closing loop: I've added the alert rule, PR is in review for cache invalidation, and postmortem draft created. We'll schedule a retro with SRE and Platform next week. :thumbsup:
